Memorial & memory-keeping (2026)

Memorialised profiles and ways to preserve stories. This page covers Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, WhatsApp: what each platform does when someone dies and how family can memorialise or remove an account.

Memorial and legacy options by platform
PlatformWhat happens
FacebookFacebook either memorialises your profile, adding 'Remembering' next to your name, or permanently deletes it, depending on what you chose in advance. A legacy contact you name can manage parts of a memorialised profile, such as a pinned tribute post, but can't log in or read your messages. Family can request memorialisation with proof of death.
InstagramInstagram memorialises an account when it receives proof of death, such as an obituary. Nobody can log into a memorialised account, and its posts stay visible to the same audience. Verified immediate family can instead ask for the account to be removed, using documents such as a death certificate. Instagram doesn't give out passwords.
X (Twitter)X doesn't memorialise accounts and won't give anyone access, including family. An immediate family member or a person authorised to act for the estate can ask X to deactivate the account. X then asks for details of the deceased, a copy of the requester's ID and a death certificate. Download your own archive now if you want posts kept.
LinkedInLinkedIn offers two options: close the account or memorialise the profile. Anyone connected or related by last name can report a member as deceased, and LinkedIn will memorialise the profile. Closing the account requires someone with legal authority to act for the estate, a death certificate and probate-type documents. LinkedIn never gives out passwords.
WhatsAppWhatsApp doesn't memorialise accounts or offer a legacy contact. Accounts are generally deleted after 365 days without connecting to WhatsApp. Chats and media saved on the person's phone stay there until the app is removed, so the phone itself is usually the only way family can keep messages. Recipients keep their own copies of messages.

Frequently asked questions

Can I memorialise a loved one's social media account?

Facebook and Instagram offer memorialisation. Other platforms mainly offer account removal. See each platform guide for the official steps.

What do I need to memorialise or close an account?

Usually proof of death, such as a death certificate or obituary, and a link to the profile. Each platform's guide lists exactly what it asks for.
